items.title: Introducing the Amazon SageMaker JumpStart Model Leaderboard
items.summary: The Amazon SageMaker JumpStart Model Leaderboard compares 70+ foundation models side by side on quality, speed, and cost, directly in SageMaker Studio. Learn what the leaderboard shows, how AWS benchmarks models, and how to go from a shortlist to a deployed model.

items.title: How Airbnb uses cost per task to operate coding agents on Amazon Bedrock
items.summary: Airbnb runs evals on real engineering tasks and uses Amazon Bedrock observability to choose models for its coding agents and control production costs. This post shows how cost per task guides model selection, why production spending can differ from eval results, and how to monitor latency, manage quotas, and attribute spend.

items.title: Design responsible AI controls for Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL
items.summary: Learn how to make RAG chatbot answers traceable with Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL, pgvector, and Amazon Bedrock Guardrails, logging sources, scores, and guardrail traces in SQL.

items.title: Private certificate authority support in Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Identity
items.summary: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Identity now supports private certificate authorities (CAs), so your agents can connect to self-hosted identity providers that use a private CA. This post shows how to issue an IdP certificate with AWS Private CA, configure a credential provider to trust it, rotate the CA, and protect the certificate.

items.title: How Salesforce is advancing global-scale model serving with cross-Region inference routing in Amazon SageMaker AI
items.summary: Learn how Salesforce uses the cross-Region inference router in Amazon SageMaker AI to turn fragmented Regional capacity into reliable model serving. Salesforce adds capacity securely across Regions and accounts while keeping its data residency commitments, and sees per request where each call was served and why.

items.title: How Social Department built culture-aware video discovery
items.summary: Social Department, an AI operating system for entertainment marketing, worked with TrackIt and AWS to build QuickSearch: single-action queries that surface shareable scenes, quotable lines, memeable frames, and trend-aligned moments across large video libraries, using TwelveLabs models on Amazon Bedrock and Amazon OpenSearch Serverless.

items.title: Connect Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway to private APIs in a hub-and-spoke network with centralized inspection
items.summary: Many enterprises run a centralized network model: one account owns every VPC and a central firewall inspects all traffic. This post shows a tested pattern for connecting Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway to private APIs and MCP servers in that model, with the VPC Lattice resource gateway in the network account so every hop crosses the firewall.

items.title: How Stretto built an AI voice agent with Amazon Nova 2 Sonic
items.summary: Stretto replaced its web-form lead capture with Tara, an AI voice agent built on Amazon Nova 2 Sonic that conducts bankruptcy intake interviews by phone and qualifies leads. See how Stretto, the AWS Generative AI Innovation Center, and CI&T designed the voice architecture, validated it for sensitive conversations, and moved it to production.

items.title: From reporting to reasoning: Getting enterprise data ready for AI agents
items.summary: A recap of the inaugural AWS Quick User Group DC meetup, where data leaders explored getting enterprise data ready for AI agents. It covers what’s new in AWS Quick, Financial Independence Group’s AI analytics journey, and hands-on app and no-code flow building.

items.title: Managed NVIDIA Dynamo on Amazon SageMaker HyperPod Inference
items.summary: Amazon SageMaker HyperPod Inference now supports NVIDIA Dynamo for distributed inference, with multi-node and disaggregated serving, KV-aware routing, and automatic fault recovery. Serve large models across many nodes without building the orchestration layer yourself.
